-- You can also use DNS-based routing to direct a portion of the traffic to the new version of the application or service.  This way, you can control the percentage of traffic that goes to the new version by adjusting the DNS records.

## Demo 2: Location-based Rollout with Istio
Demo 1 showed how to use Istio percentage based routing.  This demo will show how to use request headers to do routing.

The use case is that some web apps run on managed devices in specific physical locations, such as store POS systems or airport kiosks. To reduce the risks to each individual location, these apps require a more targeted rollout strategy.

In these distributed scenarios, we aim to do more than just gradual rollouts — we want to minimize risk at each individual location. Let’s take the airport kiosk app as an example. Some large airports may have 20–30 kiosks, while smaller ones may only have 2 or 3. If we rely solely on random weighted routing, there’s no guarantee that kiosks at smaller airports are included in the initial 10% rollout. While they might make up 10% of the global kiosk pool, they could represent 33% or even 50% of the kiosk population at a specific airport.

To assume the worst-case scenario and reduce the potential impact per location, we need a strategy that ensures each rollout phase targets 10% of kiosks at each location individually, not just globally.

Here’s an approach that can be used to achieve location-aware gradual rollouts:

- Retrieve All Kiosks
   Use an existing API to get the full list of kiosks from the database, including metadata such as airport codes.
- Group and Subdivide
In the GitHub Actions workflow, group the kiosks by airport/station code, then generate sublists representing 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40% of kiosks per location. Combined, these form a full 100% rollout plan but segmented per station.
- Beta Phase Deployment
Select the 10% sublist for the Beta phase.
- Use an API call to update the release version (either blue or green) for the selected kiosks.
Note: If a station has fewer than 10 kiosks, only those meeting the rollout threshold are included. For example, a station with just 1 kiosk is excluded in the Beta phase, since deploying there would already exceed the 10% threshold.

- Client-Side Version Awareness
A service worker in the frontend app loads the kiosk profile after each session.
When it detects a version change, the front end app fetches the new release version from the profile and includes it in every HTTP request header.

5. Traffic Routing via Istio

An Istio VirtualService inspects the release field in the http header.
If the release version is blue, traffic is routed to the blue deployment. If green, then to the green deployment.

7. Rollout Progression

For each rollout phase, the next percentage sublist (20%, 30%, etc.) is processed.
The update API sets the release version appropriately to gradually move towards 100% rollout across all stations.
